comparisons.peer_topic: Hazardous substance and environmental regulations in manufacturing
comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor manufacturing and R&D operations are regulated under laws governing health, safety, and the environment, including pollutant discharge limits, chemical content restrictions (e.g., lead), and waste management, with specific legislative impacts from the U.S., EU, and China.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose environmental compliance and waste management obligations in Item 1, though Intel focuses on internal circular economy strategies and specific recycling targets, while Broadcom focuses on the regulatory risks and restrictions imposed by external laws. Intel explicitly links waste management goals to executive incentives, whereas Broadcom details the specific environmental regulations (e.g., lead restrictions, discharge limits) that govern its manufacturing operations without citing specific internal performance targets in this item.

sentences.text: We have long been committed to waste management, recycling, and circular economy strategies that enable the recovery and productive re-use of waste streams.
In 2024, we linked a portion of our executive and employee performance bonus to our interim target to achieve a greater than 90% recycling rate of construction waste.

Our semiconductor manufacturing operations and research and development involve the use of hazardous substances and are regulated under international, federal, state and local laws governing health, safety and the environment.

These regulations include limitations on discharge of pollutants to air, water, and soil; remediation requirements; product chemical content limitations; manufacturing chemical use and handling restrictions; pollution control requirements; waste minimization considerations; and treatment, transport, storage and disposal of solid and hazardous wastes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Executive Compensation Link to Human Capital
comparisons.peer_summary: Progress towards human capital advancements serves as a non-financial performance modifier for fiscal 2024 executive bonuses, adjusting payout by a multiple of 0.9 to 1.1.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose the linkage of executive compensation to non-financial or specific performance targets in Item 1. Intel explicitly links a portion of executive and employee performance bonuses to an interim environmental target (>90% recycling rate of construction waste), whereas Qualcomm links executive bonuses to 'human capital advancements' via a non-financial performance modifier. Both demonstrate the use of Item 1 to highlight executive incentive structures tied to operational or human capital goals, rather than solely financial metrics.
